newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO OPEN PROCEEDINGS AGAINST TOSHACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO OPEN PROCEEDINGS AGAINST TOSHACK.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna have opened disciplinary proceedings against John Toshack after the Welshman insulted fans who were barracking him for substituting Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo in Sunday's game against Athletic Bilbao.

"Although (people) were very nervous in the stadium, the coach's attitude cannot be forgiven and must be criticized," said Deportivo president Augusto Lendoiro, who had tried to calm his players and coach at half-time.
In an interview published in the sports daily As on Tuesday, Toshack said he was not considering resigning and that he hoped the hearings would clarify the incident.
"My insults and gestures were aimed only and exclusively at a section of the crowd that feels that ... I am the only one to blame for what happens at the club," he said.
"I've put up with insults for a long time, but the reaction was not normal for me," the former Liverpool striker said.
The dressing-room discontent at Deportivo was evident at Monday's training session, when Rivaldo and Toshack avoided speaking to each other.
The incidents are the last in a long series of clashes between Toshack and the Riazor crowd since his arrival at Deportivo last season.
Fans were especially angered by his decision to drop Bebeto, and blamed Toshack for the striker's subsequent move back to Brazil.

For his part, Toshack has blamed Lendoiro for buying the wrong players and not spending enough on infrastructure and training facilities. Earlier this year he said he did not expect to continue at the club when his contract expires in June.
Supporters replied swiftly by daubing the Riazor ground in anti-Toshack grafitti, some written in English.

Toshack has also come under fire from Rafael Martin Vazquez. The former Spanish international midfielder is one of many players in Deportivo's star-studded squad who believes he is not selected often enough.

The Spanish media has also lashed out at what they see as Toshack's negative tactics and poor use of gifted players. After the game against Barcelona one commentator described him as an 'alchemist' because of his 'ability to turn gold into lead'.
